tooltip.title: Bullous Pemphigoid (BP)
tooltip.markdown: The most common autoimmune blistering disease, typically affecting the elderly. Characterized by tense bullae and intense pruritus.

tooltip.title: Pathophysiology of BP
tooltip.markdown: Understanding the molecular mechanisms of bullous pemphigoid

tooltip.title: Target Antigens
tooltip.markdown: Autoantibodies (IgG) against hemidesmosomal proteins BP180 (Type XVII Collagen) and BP230

tooltip.title: Mechanism
tooltip.markdown: Antibody binding at the basement membrane zone (BMZ) activates complement and recruits eosinophils and neutrophils, leading to separation

tooltip.title: Blister Level
tooltip.markdown: Subepidermal split

tooltip.title: Clinical Features of BP
tooltip.markdown: Key clinical manifestations and physical findings

tooltip.title: Prodrome
tooltip.markdown: Intense pruritus and urticarial or eczematous plaques may precede blisters by weeks to months

tooltip.title: Cutaneous Bullae
tooltip.markdown: Large, tense bullae on erythematous or urticarial skin. Rupture leads to erosions that heal without scarring

tooltip.title: Nikolsky Sign
tooltip.markdown: Negative

tooltip.title: Distribution
tooltip.markdown: Trunk, flexural areas, and extremities

tooltip.title: Diagnosis of BP
tooltip.markdown: Diagnostic tests and findings

tooltip.title: Histology
tooltip.markdown: Subepidermal blister with an eosinophil-rich infiltrate

tooltip.title: Direct Immunofluorescence
tooltip.markdown: Linear deposition of IgG and C3 along the BMZ

tooltip.title: Salt-Split Skin
tooltip.markdown: Antibody binding to the roof (epidermal side) of the split

tooltip.title: Serology
tooltip.markdown: Positive ELISA for anti-BP180 and/or anti-BP230 antibodies

tooltip.title: Treatment of BP
tooltip.markdown: Therapeutic approaches for bullous pemphigoid

tooltip.title: First Line - Topical
tooltip.markdown: High-potency topical corticosteroids (e.g., Clobetasol) are preferred

tooltip.title: First Line - Oral
tooltip.markdown: Systemic steroids (Prednisone) or Doxycycline are alternatives

tooltip.title: Adjuvant Therapy
tooltip.markdown: Methotrexate, Mycophenolate, Azathioprine

tooltip.title: Refractory Disease Treatment
tooltip.markdown: Rituximab, Dupilumab, Omalizumab, IVIG
